concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which body was established to control all matters of civil and military government of British territories in India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Board of Control**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Board of Control** was established under the **Pitt's India Act of 1784**.
 
• This act was introduced to ensure better governance of the **British territories in India**.
 
• The board had the authority to oversee and direct all matters related to the **civil and military government** in British India.
 
• It functioned alongside the **Court of Directors of the East India Company**, ensuring a balance between the British Crown and the Company.
 
• The Board of Control consisted of **six members**, including the **Chancellor of the Exchequer** and the **Secretary of State**.
 
• It was responsible for formulating policies related to **administration, trade, and military** in India.
 
• This mechanism marked a significant shift, as it gave the British Crown greater control over the **Company's affairs** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Board of Legislature**__

 __
 
• This term does not refer to any specific historical or administrative body related to British India.
 
• It might signify a legislative assembly or governing body responsible for enacting laws, but it is not related to the governance structure established under the **Pitt's India Act.**
 
 
 
• **Board of Executives**__
 __
 
• No official body named **Board of Executives** existed in the context of British India.
 
• The term could refer to an executive committee or governing body in general, but it is not relevant to the governance mechanism established by the British Crown for India.
 
 
 
• **Board of Directors**__
 
 
• The **Board of Directors** was part of the East India Company and responsible for managing the company's business affairs.
 
• While it played a key role in trade and commercial decisions, it did not oversee matters of **civil and military governance.**
 
• Under the **Pitt's India Act**, the Board of Directors worked alongside the Board of Control, with the latter having greater authority over governance matters.
